logline: Morpheus, the ageless lord of dreams, escapes a century of occult imprisonment and must rebuild his shattered realm while gradually confronting what his own cold perfection has cost him and the people around him.

renewal.note: Season 2, released in parts from July 3, 2025, concluded the series. Neil Gaiman's sexual misconduct allegations surfaced in 2024 and complicated the show's promotion, though Netflix completed the second season.

bollymeter.basis: 88% on Rotten Tomatoes from 122 critics; widely credited as a faithful, visually rich adaptation that proved the 'unadaptable' Gaiman comic could work on screen, with particular praise for Tom Sturridge's centred lead performance.

pull_quotes.text: The spirit is the same: an elegant representation that serves and enhances the storytelling.
The first season of The Sandman is a stunning adaptation that faithfully brings to life its multitude of eccentric characters.

seasons.review_body: Season 1 dropped August 5, 2022 with 10 episodes plus a special episode on August 19. An 88-percent Rotten Tomatoes score from 122 critics stands out given the source material's reputation for unfilmability. The adaptation keeps close fidelity to the comic's spirit. The season clusters around three strengths: the visual design of the Dreaming, Tom Sturridge's internally complex lead performance, and the anthology structure that allows individual episodes to function as self-contained short films within a larger arc. The show works best when it diverges from Morpheus to deepen supporting characters and arcs. A special episode adapting two short story collections reads as a formal experiment within a streaming context.

episode_reviews.title: The Sound of Her Wings
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The sixth episode pauses the main plot to spend most of its runtime with Death, Morpheus's older sister, as she guides souls through their final day. Kirby Howell-Baptiste's performance reconfigured the season: Death is warm, practical, and genuinely compassionate where Morpheus is cool and formal. The episode is the emotional centre of Season 1 and a standalone argument for what the show could be.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Death meets the old man who has lived a hundred years trying to avoid her - a short scene that contains the entire season's meditation on mortality.

episode_reviews.title: And Dreaming I Was Dreaming
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The bonus special episode adapts two Gaiman stories from outside the main comics arc, demonstrating the anthology range the source material contains. A two-hander with Morpheus and Hob Gadling, a man granted immortality to test whether humans truly want eternal life, stands as the episode's finest hour.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Hob and Morpheus's centuries-spanning pub meeting, where the terms of their friendship are finally stated honestly.

bollymeter.basis: 74% on Rotten Tomatoes from 38 critics; a visually consistent continuation that critics found over-compressed and emotionally rushed compared to Season 1's more patient storytelling.

pull_quotes.text: It's frustrating how abridged this all is, how Morpheus got ten episodes of moping.
As visually gorgeous and heartfelt as it can be, The Sandman does push the limits.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 released in three tranches across July 2025, adapting the second half of Gaiman's comics arc as the show moved toward its conclusion. A 74-percent Rotten Tomatoes score from 38 reviews marked a step back from Season 1's 88 percent, with compression identified as the central problem. The season can feel like material that needed Season 1's patience has been pushed through a truncated arc. Visually, it stays consistent, but the story carries strains. The 12-episode count spread across multiple release windows also dilutes the narrative momentum Season 1 built week-to-week. The show remains ambitious and periodically beautiful, but the adaptation ultimately runs up against the limits of what a streaming format can accommodate from source material this dense.
seasons.season_over_season: Narrative compression that Season 1 avoided becomes the defining critical complaint; the visual and performance quality holds but the storytelling pacing slips.
